identity.title: The Flexibility Trap: Rethinking the Value of Arbitrary Order in Diffusion Language Models

problem.claim: The paper examines whether arbitrary-order token generation improves reasoning in diffusion language models (dLLMs), particularly on mathematics and coding tasks.

gap.claim: The authors report that arbitrary-order generation can limit reasoning potential because dLLMs may bypass high-uncertainty tokens needed for exploration, causing premature collapse of solution coverage.

contributions.claim: Identifies a flexibility trap in which dLLM order flexibility may undermine exploration during reasoning.
Introduces JustGRPO, which forgoes arbitrary-order generation and applies standard GRPO while retaining parallel decoding.
Reports that this minimalist approach can elicit effective reasoning, including 89.1% accuracy on GSM8K.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish JustGRPO as a minimalist way to train dLLMs for reasoning by abandoning arbitrary order while preserving parallel decoding.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report 89.1% accuracy on GSM8K with JustGRPO.
The authors report that JustGRPO fully retains dLLM parallel decoding ability despite forgoing arbitrary order.
The authors observe that dLLMs tend to avoid high-uncertainty tokens crucial for exploration, leading to premature solution-coverage collapse.

narrative_sequence.summary: dLLMs permit arbitrary token-generation orders, seemingly expanding the solution space beyond fixed autoregressive trajectories.
For general reasoning, the authors report that this flexibility may instead reduce reasoning potential by bypassing uncertain but important tokens.
This observation motivates reconsidering RL methods that incur complexity to preserve arbitrary-order flexibility.
JustGRPO simply uses standard GRPO without arbitrary order and is reported to achieve strong reasoning performance while retaining parallel decoding.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a nominally larger generation space to a behavioral tendency to avoid high-uncertainty exploratory tokens, then aligns the training objective with the simpler fixed-order choice.

lessons.interpretation: A broader action space may be counterproductive when the model learns shortcuts that reduce exploratory coverage.
lessons.application: When proposing a flexible generation or planning mechanism, explicitly test whether it preserves exploration of uncertain intermediate decisions; if not, compare against a deliberately constrained training variant.
lessons.exception: This move may be unsuitable when arbitrary order is itself essential to the target task or when exploration can be measured and preserved by another mechanism.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify JustGRPO’s full training and decoding procedure, baselines, evaluation settings, or comparative results beyond the GSM8K accuracy figure.

The reported mechanism and performance are attributed to the authors; the abstract does not provide evidence sufficient to assess causal validity, reproducibility, or generalization beyond the mentioned reasoning tasks.
